parameters.name: rollout lead point - 45 deg or greater bank
parameters.verbatim: As a guide, during composite flight use a 10° lead point for turns with 45° or greater bank .

parameters.name: rollout lead point - less than 45 deg bank
parameters.verbatim: Use a 5° lead point for turns with less than 45° bank.

parameters.name: steep turn power
parameters.value: power increase required to maintain airspeed
parameters.verbatim: For steep turns, a power increase is required to maintain airspeed.

parameters.name: precision turn example
parameters.value: precise 90 degree turn using a road or section line
parameters.verbatim: To make a precise 90 degree turn, align the A/C with a road or section line on the ground, and turn perpendicular to it.

procedure_steps: Clear in the direction of the turn.
Simultaneously apply aileron and rudder pressure in the direction of the turn; hold control pressure constant until at the desired angle of bank.
Keep the bug spot on or near the horizon; as bank increases, increase backpressure and raise the bug spot to slightly above the horizon.
Approaching the desired angle of bank, return ailerons and rudder to neutral but maintain the increased pitch attitude to hold constant altitude.
For steep turns, add power to maintain airspeed.
To roll out, apply aileron and rudder pressure toward the high wing and release elevator pressure smoothly as bank decreases, keeping the bug spot on the horizon.
Start the rollout before the desired heading using a 10 degree lead for 45 degrees or greater bank and a 5 degree lead for less than 45 degrees bank.
For a precision turn, align the A/C with a road or section line on the ground and turn perpendicular to it; in the absence of a ground reference, pick a point on the horizon directly off a wingtip.
common_errors: A common error is to treat a steep turn differently from a shallow turn. The aerodynamic effects are more pronounced in a steep turn, but ultimately the same as in any turn. The difference between steep turns and shallow turns is the amount of back stick pressure and power needed to maintain level flight.
Rapid and abrupt control inputs often result in excessive backpressure (causing a climb) or insufficient backpressure (causing a dive).
Constantly leaning forward, backward, or side-to-side changes the relative position of A/C references with respect to outside references.

Rolling out without lead: because the A/C normally turns as long as there is bank, the A/C continues to turn during the rollout until the wings return to the level position; the steeper the bank, the more lead is required.
corrections: To correct nose-low (or nose-high) attitudes in a steep turn, reduce (or increase) the angle of bank with coordinated aileron and rudder pressure. Simultaneously adjust backpressure to raise (or lower) the nose to the desired pitch attitude. After attaining the desired attitude, re-establish the desired angle of bank.
As a technique, crosscheck the VSI to detect nose-low or nose-high attitudes.
Maintain a consistent position in the cockpit so outside references remain the same.
sections.notes: Bug spot = a point on the windscreen directly in front of the pilot that appears to pivot on the horizon. Dragging the IFF TRANSPONDER antenna across the horizon is another T-6 reference commonly used to maintain a level turn. The best outside reference for measuring bank is the angle of the horizon across the windscreen.

sections.title: ADVERSE YAW
sections.technique_summary: Adverse yaw is the tendency of the A/C to yaw away from the direction of aileron input. Increased lift on the up-going wing causes more induced drag, which retards forward movement of that wing, resulting in the nose yawing opposite the direction of the roll. Adverse yaw is eliminated by use of the rudder: as aileron pressure is applied, simultaneously apply rudder pressure in the same direction as the desired turn, and use rudder pressure as long as the bank is changing.

parameters.name: rudder pressure requirement
parameters.value: depends on A/C speed and amount of aileron deflection
parameters.verbatim: The correct amount of rudder pressure depends on the A/C speed and the amount of aileron deflection.

procedure_steps: As aileron pressure is applied, simultaneously apply rudder pressure in the same direction as the desired turn.
Use rudder pressure as long as the bank is changing.
Crosscheck the turn and slip indicator and keep the ball centered.
Use rudder in the same direction as aileron control stick pressure during the roll out as well as the entry.
common_errors: Failing to use rudder with aileron, allowing the nose to yaw opposite the direction of the roll.
Aileron drag effect is present during recovery from a turn as well as during the entry; not using rudder in the roll out leaves adverse yaw uncountered.
corrections: A common technique is to step / kick on the ball. This means to push on the rudder that is on the same side of centerline as the ball so as to put the ball back in the middle of the turn and slip indicator.

sections.title: UNCOORDINATED FLIGHT
sections.technique_summary: In a coordinated level turn with constant bank and airspeed, the flight path of the A/C is a true circle (no wind). Variation in the circular flight path is caused by uncoordinated control, erratic bank, or changes in airspeed. A skid is caused by insufficient bank angle in relation to the turn rate; a slip is caused by too much bank angle in relation to the turn rate.
common_errors: A skid is caused by insufficient bank angle in relation to the turn rate of the A/C. Excessive bottom rudder (rudder deflection to the inside of the turn) during the turn causes a skid.

A skid also occurs in level flight if the nose of the A/C rotates sideways about the vertical axis when the wings are held level due to improper rudder input. The result is a slow turn caused by the rudder only.
Skids are dangerous due to the possibility of inadvertent roll at slow airspeeds.
A slip is caused by too much bank angle in relation to the turn rate of the A/C. When in a turn, insufficient bottom rudder pressure in relation to the aileron pressure results in a slip.
A slip can be induced by holding opposite rudder in a turn.
Variation in the circular flight path is also caused by uncoordinated control, erratic bank, or changes in airspeed.
corrections: Slips are used to align the A/C with the runway for landing during crosswind conditions. Slips are also useful for increasing descent rates in certain situations.
sections.notes: Figure 2.8 Coordinated and Uncoordinated Flight. Source wording for the skid indication reads 'The turn-and-slip ball shows a slip by displacing to the outside of the turn' inside paragraph 2.12.2 (skid); paragraph 2.12.3 states the slip indication is the ball displacing to the inside of the turn. Recorded as printed.

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.technique_summary: Chapter 3 establishes the standard for all ground operations. The manual frames ground operations as foundational: "Mastery of ground operations is an important first step towards mastery in the air."
sections.notes: Chapter 3 of this manual does not use the formal "Common Errors" subsection format found in later chapters (e.g. 5.x). Entries below record the manual's explicit prohibitions and cautions ("do not...", "avoid...", "use caution...") as common_errors, near-verbatim; nothing is inferred beyond the text.

sections.title: PRE-FLIGHT CHECK
sections.technique_summary: Pre-flight checks start before reaching the A/C. Survey taxi routes for potential hazards such as foreign objects, repair work, stray equipment, vehicles, or personnel. Take note of fuelling or other A/C servicing that may impact preflight checks or engine start. Inform maintenance of special requirements as soon as possible.
procedure_steps: Survey taxi routes for potential hazards (foreign objects, repair work, stray equipment, vehicles, personnel) before reaching the A/C.
Note fuelling or other A/C servicing that may impact preflight checks or engine start.
Inform maintenance of special requirements as soon as possible (for example, oil requirements for cross-country, seat tie-up for solo, position in formation).
common_errors: Failing to inform maintenance of special requirements as soon as possible (oil requirements for cross-country, seat tie-up for solo, position in formation).
Not surveying the taxi route for hazards before reaching the A/C.

sections.title: A/C FORMS
sections.technique_summary: The Air Force Technical Order (AFTO) Form 781 is the official log of A/C operation, servicing, and maintenance. Check the form before any A/C inspection, other action, or checklist is initiated. Contact maintenance to report discrepancies in the form or for clarification.

parameters.name: aircraft forms document
parameters.verbatim: The Air Force Technical Order (AFTO) Form 781 is the official log of A/C operation, servicing, and maintenance.

procedure_steps: Check the AFTO Form 781 before any A/C inspection, other action, or checklist is initiated.
Contact maintenance to report discrepancies in the form or for clarification.
Do not accept the A/C until the form is accurate and there is no question regarding the acceptability of the A/C.
common_errors: Initiating an A/C inspection, other action, or checklist before checking the forms.
Accepting the A/C while the form is inaccurate or while there is a question regarding the acceptability of the A/C.
corrections: Contact maintenance to report discrepancies in the form or for clarification.
Do not accept the A/C until the form is accurate and there is no question regarding the acceptability of the A/C.

sections.title: BEFORE EXTERIOR INSPECTION
sections.technique_summary: Before turning on the battery, ensure that cockpit switches are positioned properly and that the prop area is clear. It is good technique to pre-adjust straps and pre-position personal equipment and publications to expedite strap-in. Take precautions when pre-positioning or stowing equipment or pubs in the cockpit.
procedure_steps: Before turning on the battery, ensure cockpit switches are positioned properly and the prop area is clear.
Pre-adjust straps and pre-position personal equipment and publications to expedite strap-in.
Stow personal gear not required to execute the mission in the baggage compartment.
common_errors: Turning on the battery before ensuring cockpit switches are positioned properly and the prop area is clear.
Placing anything on the canopy glass (causes damage): "Do not place anything on the canopy glass to prevent damage."
Stowing clothing or miscellaneous personal items in the cockpit: "Do not stow clothing or miscellaneous personal items in the cockpit."
Stowing items so that they interfere with the ejection or any other system.
corrections: Stow personal gear, not required to execute the mission, in the baggage compartment.
Use caution when stowing items to prevent interference with the ejection or any other system.

sections.title: EXTERIOR INSPECTION
sections.technique_summary: A thorough walk around of the A/C is a critical part of each mission. Maintenance performs detailed inspections and prepares the A/C for flight; however, the pilot's walk around serves as a last look before flight. During the Exterior Inspection, you must wear your flight gloves. The pilot in command has final authority to accept or reject an A/C.

parameters.name: walk around start point and direction
parameters.verbatim: The walk around checklist begins behind the left wing and moves about the A/C in a clockwise direction.

parameters.name: required personal equipment
parameters.verbatim: During the Exterior Inspection, you must wear your flight gloves.

procedure_steps: Begin the walk around behind the left wing and move about the A/C in a clockwise direction.
It is not necessary to refer to the checklist for each item, but reference the checklist to ensure all items are completed.
Carefully check for fluid leaks in the wheel well, speed brake, and engine bay areas; fluid along fairing doors, seams, and line couplings may indicate potential leaks.
Check the general condition of trim tabs, hinges, and control surfaces.
Ensure that tire condition is acceptable for the planned mission.
common_errors: Not wearing flight gloves during the Exterior Inspection.
Manhandling control surfaces: "do not manhandle control surfaces."
Missing fluid leaks in the wheel well, speed brake, and engine bay areas; fluid along fairing doors, seams, and line couplings may indicate potential leaks.
Failing to reference the checklist to ensure all items are completed.
Accepting tire condition that is not acceptable for the planned mission.
corrections: If you are unsure about the condition or operation of any system, check with qualified maintenance personnel.

sections.title: SEATING POSITION IN THE A/C
sections.technique_summary: Sitting position should be the same on every flight. When sitting comfortably the upper part of the EADI display should be visible just below the glare shield. Adjust the rudder pedals to allow full travel of the rudder and brakes, and during strap-in ensure there is enough length with minimal slack in the leg restraint lines for full rudder deflection.

parameters.name: seat height reference (EADI)
parameters.value: upper part of the EADI display visible just below the glare shield
parameters.verbatim: When sitting comfortably the upper part of the EADI display should be visible just below the glare shield.

parameters.name: helmet-to-canopy clearance
parameters.verbatim: At least one fist separation between the top of the helmet and the canopy ensures adequate clearance for the canopy breaker during ejection.

parameters.name: rudder pedal adjustment
parameters.value: full travel of the rudder and brakes
parameters.verbatim: Adjust the rudder pedals to allow full travel of the rudder and brakes.

parameters.name: leg restraint lines
parameters.value: enough length with minimal slack for full rudder deflection
parameters.verbatim: During strap in, ensure there is enough length with minimal slack in the leg restraint lines for full rudder deflection.

procedure_steps: Set the same sitting position on every flight.
Adjust seat height so the upper part of the EADI display is visible just below the glare shield when sitting comfortably.
Verify at least one fist separation between the top of the helmet and the canopy.
Adjust the rudder pedals to allow full travel of the rudder and brakes.
During strap-in, set leg restraint lines with enough length and minimal slack for full rudder deflection.
common_errors: Sitting position not the same on every flight.
Less than one fist separation between the top of the helmet and the canopy — inadequate clearance for the canopy breaker during ejection.
Rudder pedals not adjusted to allow full travel of the rudder and brakes.
Leg restraint lines too short or with excessive slack, preventing full rudder deflection.

sections.title: COCKPIT ORGANIZATION
sections.technique_summary: The T-6 cockpit has limited storage space, so good cockpit organization is essential. Cockpit organization varies by mission and personal preference. In-flight publications or FLIP should be readily available; one technique is to organize them in the order in which they will be used.
procedure_steps: Keep in-flight publications or FLIP readily available.
As a technique, organize publications in the order in which they will be used.
common_errors: Large checklists or other items on the left leg may cause interference with PCL movement or cause inadvertent radio transmissions.
In-flight publications or FLIP not readily available.

sections.title: INTERIOR INSPECTION
sections.technique_summary: Ensure the propeller area is clear before turning the battery on or starting/motoring the engine. Pre-solo student pilots will verbalize each item in the interior inspection checklist.

parameters.name: verbalization requirement
parameters.value: pre-solo students verbalize each checklist item
parameters.verbatim: Pre-solo student pilots will verbalize each item in the interior inspection checklist.

procedure_steps: Ensure the propeller area is clear before turning the battery on or starting/motoring the engine.
Pre-solo student pilots verbalize each item in the interior inspection checklist.
common_errors: Turning the battery on or starting/motoring the engine without ensuring the propeller area is clear.
Pre-solo student not verbalizing each item in the interior inspection checklist.

sections.title: ENGINE START
sections.technique_summary: Ensure the canopy fracture system (CFS) pin storage box located over the left shoulder of the pilot in the RCP is closed before closing the canopy. During engine start, closely monitor interstage turbine temperature (ITT), gas generator speed (N1), and the start ready light, glancing outside occasionally to detect possible A/C movement or crew chief signals. Inform the crew chief before activating any system that could endanger ground personnel.

parameters.name: engine start monitored parameters
parameters.verbatim: During engine start; closely monitor interstage turbine temperature (ITT), gas generator speed (N1), and the start ready light.

parameters.name: CFS pin storage box
parameters.value: closed before closing the canopy (over left shoulder of RCP pilot)
parameters.verbatim: Ensure the canopy fracture system (CFS) pin storage box located over the left shoulder of the pilot in the RCP is closed before closing the canopy.

parameters.name: motoring with canopy
parameters.value: may be executed with the canopy open
parameters.verbatim: Motoring may be executed with the canopy open.

procedure_steps: Ensure the CFS pin storage box over the left shoulder of the RCP pilot is closed before closing the canopy.
During start, closely monitor ITT, N1, and the start ready light.
Occasionally glance outside to detect possible A/C movement or signals from the crew chief.
If motoring the engine before engine start is necessary, inform the crew chief and ensure the propeller area is clear (motoring may be executed with the canopy open).
Inform the crew chief before activating any system (engine start, speed brake, flaps, etc.) that could endanger ground personnel; use visual signals in accordance with T-6A S.O.P. and this manual.
The crew chief repeats the signal when it is safe to operate the system.
common_errors: Closing the canopy without ensuring the CFS pin storage box in the RCP is closed.
Failing to closely monitor ITT, N1, and the start ready light during engine start.
Remaining head-down inside — not glancing outside to detect possible A/C movement or crew chief signals.
Motoring the engine without informing the crew chief and without ensuring the propeller area is clear.
Activating a system (engine start, speed brake, flaps, etc.) that could endanger ground personnel without informing the crew chief.

Operating a system before the crew chief repeats the signal indicating it is safe. [inferred — the manual states this descriptively: "The crew chief repeats the signal when it is safe to operate the system."]
sections.notes: The last common error is inferred, not a recorded prohibition: 3.6.4 states descriptively that "The crew chief repeats the signal when it is safe to operate the system."

sections.title: OBOGS CHECK
sections.technique_summary: It is critical to check oxygen connections to ensure system integrity from the supply to the mask. Don the oxygen mask and check the anti-suffocation valve by ensuring you can breathe (expect some resistance). Verify the supply lever is on and the concentration lever is normal, then check the mask seal by selecting EMERGENCY and momentarily holding your breath. A good mask seal is indicated by a no-flow indication on the regulator (black).

parameters.name: supply lever
parameters.verbatim: verify that the supply lever is on and the concentration lever is normal

parameters.name: concentration lever
parameters.verbatim: verify that the supply lever is on and the concentration lever is normal

parameters.name: mask seal check selection
parameters.verbatim: Check the mask seal by selecting EMERGENCY and momentarily holding your breath.

parameters.name: good mask seal indication
parameters.verbatim: A good mask seal is indicated by a no-flow indication on the regulator (black).

parameters.name: verbal challenge
parameters.verbatim: PF verbally challenge the other crewmember with “on, normal, normal, good blinker.”

procedure_steps: Check oxygen connections to ensure system integrity from the supply to the mask.
Don the oxygen mask and check the anti-suffocation valve by ensuring you can breathe (expect some resistance).
Verify the supply lever is on and the concentration lever is normal.
Check the mask seal by selecting EMERGENCY and momentarily holding your breath; a good seal gives a no-flow (black) indication on the regulator.
PF verbally challenges the other crewmember with "on, normal, normal, good blinker."
common_errors: Not checking oxygen connections for system integrity from the supply to the mask.
Omitting the anti-suffocation valve check (ensuring you can breathe, expecting some resistance).
Not verifying supply lever on and concentration lever normal.
Omitting the mask seal check with EMERGENCY selected, or not confirming the no-flow (black) indication.
PF not verbally challenging the other crewmember with "on, normal, normal, good blinker."

sections.title: RADIO PROCEDURES
sections.technique_summary: Contact Ch-2 for taxi instructions and listen carefully to taxi instructions. Read back of the ATC clearance is always required, because it ensures understanding. Reading back instructions is also a good idea if they appear to be different than standard or appear unusual.

parameters.name: channel for taxi instructions
parameters.verbatim: Contact Ch-2 for taxi instructions and listen carefully to taxi instructions.

procedure_steps: Contact Ch-2 for taxi instructions.
Listen carefully to taxi instructions.
Read back the ATC clearance (always required).
Read back instructions that appear different than standard or unusual.
common_errors: Not reading back the ATC clearance — read back is always required because it ensures understanding.
Not listening carefully to taxi instructions.
Failing to read back instructions that appear different than standard or appear unusual.

sections.title: TAXI
sections.technique_summary: When the Before-Taxi Checklist is complete, clear the apron carefully, then signal the crew chief with the pull chocks signal in accordance with T-6A S.O.P. Select nose wheel steering (NWS), release brakes, and increase power as necessary; follow the marshaller's signals, taxi straight ahead, and check the brakes. Taxi on the centerline, apply the brakes smoothly, evenly, and cautiously at all times, and prepare for takeoff and departure while taxiing in uncongested areas.

parameters.name: taxi power setting
parameters.verbatim: Normally idle power is sufficient to initiate taxi. ... Once the A/C is rolling, idle power setting should provide sufficient power.

parameters.name: power for NWS turn
parameters.verbatim: To turn with NWS selected, simultaneously apply rudder in the desired direction and reduce power (normally to idle).

parameters.name: taxi speed
parameters.verbatim: Taxi speed is defined by LAP.

parameters.name: taxi line position (centerline)
parameters.verbatim: Taxi on the centerline.

parameters.name: staggered taxi alignment
parameters.value: align the appropriate main wheel with the taxi line; main wheel is approximately underneath the start of the wing dihedral
parameters.verbatim: If local procedures direct staggered taxi, align the appropriate main wheel with the taxi line. The main wheel is approximately underneath the start of the wing dihedral.

parameters.name: taxi speed over cables
parameters.verbatim: If a cable must be crossed, taxi as slow as possible to prevent damage to the A/C.

parameters.name: obstacle clearance / taxi interval
parameters.verbatim: Maintain obstacle clearance and taxi interval distance in accordance with Local Directives.

parameters.name: taxi checklist completion point
parameters.verbatim: Normally, the taxi checklist including NWS, brakes, and heading, turn, or slip indicators is completed on the first turn out of parking.

procedure_steps: Complete the Before-Taxi Checklist, clear the apron carefully, then signal the crew chief with the pull chocks signal (T-6A S.O.P.) when ready to taxi.
Use caution for personnel, ground equipment and foreign objects.
Select NWS, release brakes, and increase power as necessary.
Follow the marshaller's signals, taxi straight ahead, and check the brakes.
Transfer A/C control to the other pilot so he/she can check their brakes, then transfer A/C control back if desired.
Complete the taxi checklist (NWS, brakes, and heading, turn, or slip indicators) normally on the first turn out of parking.
To turn with NWS selected, simultaneously apply rudder in the desired direction and reduce power (normally to idle).
For a sharper turn, deselect NWS (nose wheel casters freely) and use the inside brake to turn.
Taxi on the centerline, or align the appropriate main wheel with the taxi line if local procedures direct staggered taxi.
Techniques to establish this stagger include aligning the taxi line just outside of the canopy rail and lining up the exhaust stack on the taxi line.
Prepare for takeoff and departure while taxiing in uncongested areas (WX, winds, departure routing, NAVAID setup, takeoff emergencies), using the acronym included in the SOPs.
common_errors: Riding the brakes: "Use the brakes as necessary to control taxi speed; however, do not ride the brakes."
Differential braking with NWS engaged: "Differential braking with the NWS engaged will wear the nose wheel steering and the tire."
Brakes not applied smoothly, evenly, and cautiously at all times.
Carrying too much power during taxi — normally idle power is sufficient to initiate taxi and once rolling idle should provide sufficient power.
Not reducing power (normally to idle) while applying rudder for an NWS turn.
Taxiing over cables: "Avoid taxiing over cables to preclude A/C damage."
Not taxiing on the centerline (or, for staggered taxi, not aligning the appropriate main wheel with the taxi line).
Failing to maintain obstacle clearance and taxi interval distance in accordance with Local Directives.
Exceeding the taxi speed defined by LAP.
Not clearing carefully for personnel, ground equipment and foreign objects.
Not completing the taxi checklist (NWS, brakes, heading/turn/slip indicators) on the first turn out of parking.
Not using uncongested taxi time to prepare for takeoff and departure (WX, winds, departure routing, NAVAID setup, takeoff emergencies).
corrections: If the A/C does not move by the release of brakes, use a small amount of extra power and retard PCL to idle again.
If a sharper turn is required, deselect NWS (the nose wheel will freely caster) and use the inside brake to turn.
If a cable must be crossed, taxi as slow as possible to prevent damage to the A/C.

sections.title: OVER SPEED GOVERNOR CHECK
sections.technique_summary: Ensure the area immediately in front of and behind the A/C is clear. During engine run-up for the overspeed governor check, the PNF guards and is ready to assume control of the brakes in case of rudder pedal rod end failure. Clear outside the A/C during this check. Power should be advanced smoothly and slowly only as high as required to verify proper function of the overspeed governor.

parameters.name: clearance requirement
parameters.value: area immediately in front of and behind the A/C clear
parameters.verbatim: Ensure area immediately in front of and behind the A/C is clear.

parameters.name: power application
parameters.value: smoothly and slowly, only as high as required to verify proper function of the overspeed governor
parameters.verbatim: Power should be advanced smoothly and slowly only as high as required to verify proper function of the overspeed governor.

parameters.name: control stick position (technique)
parameters.verbatim: As a technique, keep the control stick in the neutral to slightly aft position to prevent the nose gear strut from compressing during the check.

parameters.name: PNF duty
parameters.value: guards and is ready to assume control of the brakes
parameters.verbatim: the PNF guards and is ready to assume control of the brakes in case of rudder pedal rod end failure

procedure_steps: Ensure the area immediately in front of and behind the A/C is clear.
PNF guards and is ready to assume control of the brakes in case of rudder pedal rod end failure.
Clear outside the A/C during the check.
Advance power smoothly and slowly, only as high as required to verify proper function of the overspeed governor.
As a technique, keep the control stick neutral to slightly aft to prevent the nose gear strut from compressing during the check.
common_errors: Not ensuring the area immediately in front of and behind the A/C is clear.
Not clearing outside the A/C during the check.
Advancing power abruptly or higher than required to verify proper function of the overspeed governor.
Control stick not held neutral to slightly aft, allowing the nose gear strut to compress during the check.
PNF not guarding the brakes / not ready to assume control in case of rudder pedal rod end failure.
corrections: If the A/C moves, reduce power, pump up the brakes, and reattempt.

sections.title: BEFORE TAKEOFF AND LINEUP CHECKS
sections.technique_summary: Review takeoff and landing data (TOLD); if reported conditions are significantly different than forecast, consider using actual conditions to recompute TOLD. The Before Takeoff Checks should be executed last, right before Line Up, with no other checks or procedures executed between Before Takeoff Checks and Line Up.

parameters.name: TOLD recomputation trigger
parameters.value: reported conditions significantly different than forecast
parameters.verbatim: If reported conditions are significantly different than forecast, consider using actual conditions to recompute TOLD.

parameters.name: chain of actions
parameters.value: 1/ Before Takeoff Checks  2/ Request Line Up  3/ Line Up
parameters.verbatim: The chain of actions should be:1/ Before Takeoff Checks2/ Request Line Up3/ Line Up

procedure_steps: Review takeoff and landing data (TOLD).
If reported conditions are significantly different than forecast, consider using actual conditions to recompute TOLD.
Execute the Before Takeoff Checks last, right before Line Up.
Follow the chain: 1/ Before Takeoff Checks, 2/ Request Line Up, 3/ Line Up.
common_errors: Executing other checks or procedures between Before Takeoff Checks and Line Up: "No other checks or procedures should be executed between Before Takeoff Checks and Line Up."
Not executing the Before Takeoff Checks last, right before Line Up.
Not reviewing TOLD, or not recomputing TOLD with actual conditions when reported conditions are significantly different than forecast.
corrections: Consider using actual conditions to recompute TOLD when reported conditions differ significantly from forecast.

sections.title: AFTER LANDING
sections.technique_summary: Unless local procedures dictate otherwise, obtain clearance before crossing active runways and/or proceeding back to the ramp. Stay alert and taxi with caution. The sortie is not complete until the A/C is parked, the engine is shutdown, and all required checklist items are complete.

parameters.name: clearance requirement
parameters.value: before crossing active runways and/or proceeding back to the ramp
parameters.verbatim: Unless local procedures dictate otherwise, obtain clearance before crossing active runways and/or proceeding back to the ramp.

parameters.name: sortie completion definition
parameters.value: A/C parked, engine shutdown, all required checklist items complete
parameters.verbatim: the sortie is not complete until the A/C is parked, the engine is shutdown, and all required check-list items are complete

procedure_steps: Obtain clearance before crossing active runways and/or proceeding back to the ramp, unless local procedures dictate otherwise.
Stay alert and taxi with caution.
Complete all required checklist items; the sortie is not complete until the A/C is parked and the engine is shutdown.
common_errors: Crossing an active runway or proceeding back to the ramp without obtaining clearance.
Complacency after landing: "Do not get complacent, the sortie is not complete until the A/C is parked, the engine is shutdown, and all required check-list items are complete."
Not staying alert / not taxiing with caution after landing.

sections.title: ENGINE SHUTDOWN / BEFORE LEAVING A/C
sections.technique_summary: Keep ground personnel in sight and shut down immediately if the propeller safety zone is violated. If there is no marked propeller safety zone (for example, off-station), do not hesitate to shut down if ground personnel move too close. After exiting the cockpit, a common technique is to do an over-the-rail check before stepping down from the A/C wing.

parameters.name: over-the-rail check items
parameters.value: ejection pin and CFS pin in, ISS in SOLO, battery switch off, OBOGS lever off, parking brake as required
parameters.verbatim: Typical items include checking that the ejection pin and CFS pin are in, the ISS is in SOLO, the battery switch is off, the On Board Oxygen Generating System (OBOGS) lever is off, and the parking brake as required.

procedure_steps: Keep ground personnel in sight during shutdown.
Shut down immediately if the propeller safety zone is violated; where no zone is marked (e.g. off-station), shut down if ground personnel move too close.
After exiting the cockpit, do an over-the-rail check before stepping down from the A/C wing: ejection pin and CFS pin in, ISS in SOLO, battery switch off, OBOGS lever off, parking brake as required.
common_errors: Losing sight of ground personnel during shutdown.
Hesitating to shut down when ground personnel move too close where no propeller safety zone is marked (for example, off-station).
Stepping down from the A/C wing without doing the over-the-rail check (ejection pin and CFS pin in, ISS in SOLO, battery switch off, OBOGS lever off, parking brake as required).
corrections: Shut down immediately if the propeller safety zone is violated.

sections.title: POST FLIGHT INSPECTION
sections.technique_summary: Pilots should accomplish a post flight walk around inspection according to the checklist procedures after every sortie and report any abnormalities to maintenance. The flight manual also contains detailed strange-field procedures with post flight and pre-flight inspections for pilots to accomplish off-station if trained maintenance personnel are unavailable.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.verbatim: Pilots should accomplish a post flight walk around inspection according to the checklist procedures after every sortie

parameters.name: reportable abnormalities
parameters.value: missing panels, damaged tires, leaking fluids, bird strikes
parameters.verbatim: report any abnormalities (for example, missing panels, damaged tires, leaking fluids, bird strikes) to maintenance

procedure_steps: Accomplish a post flight walk around inspection according to checklist procedures after every sortie.
Report any abnormalities (missing panels, damaged tires, leaking fluids, bird strikes) to maintenance.
Off-station without trained maintenance personnel, use the flight manual's detailed strange-field post flight and pre-flight inspection procedures.
common_errors: Omitting the post flight walk around inspection after a sortie.
Not reporting abnormalities (missing panels, damaged tires, leaking fluids, bird strikes) to maintenance.

sections.title: ABNORMAL PROCEDURES (incl. 3.15.1 Emergency Ground Egress, 3.15.2 Return to Apron)
sections.technique_summary: Malfunctions are handled in accordance with flight manual and other applicable directives. As soon as possible, notify the controlling agency (ground or tower) if assistance is required. If maintenance or fire personnel must inspect the A/C, set the parking brake and raise both hands (hands clear) to signal that it is clear to inspect the A/C. Perform emergency ground egress in a systematic and deliberate manner; CRM is critical to a successful ground egress.

parameters.name: hands clear signal
parameters.value: set parking brake and raise both hands
parameters.verbatim: If maintenance or fire personnel must inspect the A/C, set the parking brake and raise both hands (hands clear) to signal that it is clear to inspect the A/C.

parameters.name: ISS position for ground egress
parameters.verbatim: Shut down the engine, ensure the ISS is in SOLO, and install both cockpit seat pins.

parameters.name: battery and generator timing
parameters.value: OFF just before egress (to preserve intercom with the other cockpit)
parameters.verbatim: Turn the battery and generator to OFF just before egress to preserve intercom with the other cockpit.

procedure_steps: Handle malfunctions in accordance with flight manual and other applicable directives.
Notify the controlling agency (ground or tower) as soon as possible if assistance is required.
If maintenance or fire personnel must inspect the A/C, set the parking brake and raise both hands (hands clear).
For emergency ground egress: bring the A/C to a complete stop and set the parking brake.
Shut down the engine, ensure the ISS is in SOLO, and install both cockpit seat pins.
Turn the battery and generator to OFF just before egress to preserve intercom with the other cockpit.
If returning to Apron without taking off, ensure that the After Landing Checklist items are properly executed.
common_errors: Actuating switches without informing the ground crew: "Do not actuate switches without informing the ground crew."
Not notifying the controlling agency (ground or tower) as soon as possible when assistance is required.
Performing the emergency ground egress other than in a systematic and deliberate manner.
Turning battery and generator OFF too early, losing intercom with the other cockpit before egress.
Failing to properly execute the After Landing Checklist items when returning to Apron without taking off.
Breakdown of CRM during ground egress: "CRM is critical to a successful ground egress."
sections.notes: 3.15.1 covers emergency ground egress; 3.15.2 covers returning to Apron without taking off. Both are unnamed numbered subparagraphs of 3.15 and are consolidated here. Training note (3.15.1): "This procedure may be practiced even without an emergency when leaving the cockpit."

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.technique_summary: This phase of flight is very dynamic and can be as complicated as any other part of the mission. Complex departure procedures may be required immediately after takeoff in the low altitude environment, and communications can be very busy leaving the terminal area. Emergency situations, when they occur in this phase of flight, require forethought, and quick correct action. Solid preparation is essential to success.
sections.notes: Manual heading is "4.1. Introduction"; the chapter it opens is titled "Chapter 4 — TAKEOFF, CLIMB, AND LEVEL-OFF" (title kept verbatim so it stays traceable). Chapter opener; no gradable item mapping. Printed page 47 = PDF page 57 (offset +10, not +8).

sections.title: LINEUP CHECK
sections.technique_summary: Objective is to accomplish checklist items in preparation for takeoff. This check is normally accomplished after you have stopped the A/C on the center line of the active runway. The PF must ensure that all items are complete and "BOTH" items are confirmed with the PNF. Clear final prior to crossing the runway hold short line.

parameters.name: NWS (lineup check item N)
parameters.value: Deselect after A/C aligned with RWY
parameters.verbatim: N — NWS: Deselect NWS after the A/C is aligned with the RWY

parameters.name: IFF transponder (lineup check item I)
parameters.verbatim: I — IFF transponder: NORMAL

parameters.name: Landing Light (lineup check item L)
parameters.verbatim: L — Landing Light: ON

parameters.name: Taxi Light (lineup check item T)
parameters.verbatim: T — Taxi Light: ON

parameters.name: ANTICE (lineup check item A)
parameters.verbatim: A — ANTICE: ON

parameters.name: Panel Clear (lineup check item P)
parameters.verbatim: P — Panel Clear (Only ANTI ICE is ON)

procedure_steps: Stop the A/C on the center line of the active runway.
Clear final prior to crossing the runway hold short line.
PF ensures all items are complete; "BOTH" items are confirmed with the PNF.
Run the NILTAP acronym: NWS deselect, IFF NORMAL, Landing Light ON, Taxi Light ON, ANTICE ON, Panel Clear (only ANTI ICE ON).
sections.notes: The manual gives NILTAP explicitly as "a common technique to remember the checklist steps". No common-errors block is published for this paragraph.

sections.title: TAKEOFF
sections.technique_summary: Objective is to safely get the A/C airborne. Two takeoff options exist, static and rolling. The static takeoff is used early in training because it provides more time to accomplish required checks and verify proper engine operation; a static takeoff is also required at night and for solo students. A rolling takeoff aids traffic flow in a busy pattern and is a smooth transition from taxi to takeoff roll. Rolling takeoffs have a negligible effect on TOLD and no recalculation is required.

parameters.name: engine runup torque (static takeoff)
parameters.verbatim: Clear down the runway and advance the PCL to 25 to 30 % torque.

parameters.name: power for takeoff roll
parameters.verbatim: release brakes to begin the takeoff roll and smoothly advance PCL to MAX

parameters.name: engine instrument check timing at max power
parameters.value: approximately 3 seconds after PCL reaches MAX
parameters.verbatim: Check engine instruments when stabilized at maximum power (approximately 3 seconds after PCL reaches MAX) to ensure proper operation.

parameters.name: elevator position during takeoff roll
parameters.verbatim: Position the elevator approximately neutral to prevent the nose gear from digging in during takeoff roll.

parameters.name: takeoff attitude
parameters.verbatim: smoothly apply backstick pressure to establish the takeoff attitude (approximately 7° to 10° nose high, Figure 4.1.)

parameters.name: rotation speed (no gusts)
parameters.verbatim: Without wind gusts, rotation speed is 85 KIAS.

parameters.name: rotation speed correction for gusty winds
parameters.value: increase by 1/2 the gust factor, up to 10 knot increase
parameters.verbatim: If gusty winds are present, increase rotation speed by 1/2 the gust factor (up to 10 knot increase).

procedure_steps: Check the windsock and take note of winds reported by the RSU or tower controller.
Anticipate takeoff clearance by listening to the position reports of other A/C in the pattern.
When cleared for line-up, slowly taxi to align the A/C with the runway centerline, come to a complete stop and execute the lineup check.

Static takeoff: stop aligned with the runway; pump up the brakes to prevent creep during engine runup; PNF guards the brakes (without touching rudder pedals), ready to assume control; clear down the runway and advance PCL to 25 to 30 % torque; crosscheck outside to detect creep and check engine instruments; when cleared for takeoff release brakes and smoothly advance PCL to MAX; check engine instruments when stabilized at maximum power.
Rolling takeoff: once aligned with the runway, disengage NWS and smoothly advance the PCL to MAX; check engine instruments when stabilized at maximum power.
Takeoff roll: with no crosswind, deflect the control stick slightly right to compensate for torque at MAX power; with a crosswind, deflect the control stick into the crosswind component.
Position the elevator approximately neutral; counteract the left deviation with right rudder.
Move the heels from the rudder pedals to the floor and use rudder for directional control throughout the takeoff roll.
At rotation speed (85 KIAS without gusts) smoothly apply backstick pressure to establish approximately 7° to 10° nose high.
Immediately after takeoff and safe gear retraction, apply some right rudder trim to counteract adverse yaw and center the ball.
common_errors: Making a radio call while an A/C is landing or taking off ("Do not to make a radio call while an A/C is landing or takeoff.").
A/C creep during engine runup if the brakes are not pumped up — crosscheck outside to detect creep.
Failing to deflect the control stick slightly right without crosswind, so torque generated at MAX power is not compensated.
Failing to deflect the control stick into the crosswind component, allowing the upwind wing to lift.
Elevator not approximately neutral, so the nose gear digs in during takeoff roll.
Not counteracting the A/C tendency to deviate to the left caused by power application (insufficient right rudder).
Leaving the heels on the rudder pedals, risking accidental brake application.
Using control inputs that are too large as airspeed increases — flight controls become more effective, so progressively smaller inputs are required.
Not applying right rudder trim after takeoff/safe gear retraction, leaving adverse yaw and the ball off center.
corrections: Counteract the left deviation from power application by applying right rudder.
Move the heels from the rudder pedals to the floor to prevent accidental brake application and use rudder for directional control throughout the takeoff roll.
Progressively use smaller control inputs as airspeed increases to maintain A/C control.
Technique: reduce the pitch attitude picture by half (place the spinner slightly below the horizon) to attain the takeoff attitude; use control stick pressure as necessary to hold this attitude.
Immediately after takeoff and safe gear retraction apply some right rudder trim to counteract adverse yaw and center the ball.
sections.notes: Figure 4.1 (PDF page 59) is titled "FCP Takeoff Pitch Attitude" and is image-only — no extractable numeric text beyond the 7°–10° in the body. DERIVED COMMON ERRORS: Chapter 4 publishes no "Common Errors" block (such blocks appear elsewhere, e.g. §5.35.6, PDF page 95); the common_errors listed here are derived by inverting the imperatives of the source text, each traceable to a sentence of the manual, and are not a verbatim manual list.

sections.title: CROSSWIND TAKEOFF
sections.technique_summary: The procedures for a takeoff with a crosswind are the same as for a no wind takeoff except aileron is held into the wind to keep the wings level. Aileron deflection is necessary because the upwind wing develops more lift, causing it to fly (begin rising) before the downwind wing. Anticipate the aileron requirement due to the crosswind and either preposition aileron into the wind or apply aileron into wind as required during takeoff roll. Use rudder to keep the A/C from weather-vaning.
procedure_steps: Use the same procedures as a no wind takeoff.
Hold aileron into the wind to keep the wings level.
Anticipate the aileron requirement: either preposition aileron into the wind or apply aileron into wind as required during takeoff roll.
Use rudder to keep the A/C from weather-vaning (for example, crabbing or turning into the wind).
Use progressively smaller control inputs as airspeed increases.
common_errors: Insufficient aileron into the wind, allowing the upwind wing to rise — "If the upwind wing rises skipping may result (Figure 4.2.)."

Skipping: "a series of very small bounces caused when the A/C attempts to fly on one wing and settles back onto the runway. During these bounces, the A/C moves sideways and stress on the landing gear is increased."
Allowing the A/C to weather-vane (for example, crabbing or turning into the wind) instead of holding runway alignment with rudder.
Failing to reduce control input size as airspeed increases (controls become more effective).
corrections: Anticipate aileron requirement due to the crosswind and either preposition aileron into the wind or apply aileron into wind as required during takeoff roll.
Use rudder to keep the A/C from weather-vaning.
Progressively smaller control inputs are required to maintain A/C control as airspeed increases.
sections.notes: Figure 4.2 "Skipping on Takeoff" is on PDF page 60 (printed 50) and is image-only. DERIVED COMMON ERRORS: Chapter 4 publishes no "Common Errors" block; the common_errors listed here are derived by inverting the imperatives of the source text and are not a verbatim manual list.

sections.title: AFTER BECOMING AIRBORNE
sections.technique_summary: Objective is to transition the A/C from takeoff roll to climb. Control inputs change significantly as the A/C leaves the ground; rudder requirements change as the wheels leave the ground and airspeed increases. Retract gear and flaps when safely airborne with a positive climb rate and engine instruments are checked within limits. Gear and flap retraction should be a conscious, deliberate act.

parameters.name: climb airspeed after airborne
parameters.verbatim: a. Airspeed – Accelerate to climb airspeed (140-180 KIAS)

parameters.name: power after airborne
parameters.verbatim: b. Power – Max

parameters.name: pitch after airborne
parameters.verbatim: c. Pitch – As required to fly desired airspeed (normally 10-15°)

parameters.name: landing gear and flap airspeed limit
parameters.verbatim: confirm the landing gear warning lights are extinguished and the flaps are up before the landing gear and flap airspeed limit of 147KIAS

parameters.name: maximum climb rate airspeed / pitch
parameters.value: 140 KIAS, nose as high as 12° above the horizon
parameters.verbatim: Although the maximum climb rate occurs at 140 KIAS with the nose as high as 12° above the horizon

parameters.name: normal climb-out airspeed
parameters.verbatim: normally accelerate to 16 0-180 KIAS during climb out to allow the nose to be lower to improve forward visibility

procedure_steps: Retract gear and flaps when safely airborne with a positive climb rate and engine instruments checked within limits.
Before moving the gear handle, the PF makes an intercockpit "gear clear" / gear up call and pauses momentarily.
On student presolo contact sorties the IP must acknowledge the "gear clear" call with "clear" before the student pilot raises the gear; on all other sorties "gear clear" is an advisory call only.
After gear and flap retraction, confirm the landing gear warning lights are extinguished and the flaps are up before 147 KIAS.
Check that the engine instruments are within limits.
As airspeed increases, apply nose-down trim to relieve pressure on the control stick.
Technique: PF verbalizes "climbing, good engine, gear clear" prior to raising the gear and flaps; PNF may respond "clear" once verifying safely airborne and climbing.
Verify climbing by altimeter and VSI indications; monitor torque and ITT within tolerances.

Technique for cleanup confirmation: PF says "Gear and flaps up at (read airspeed) below 147 KIAS" — gear up: gear handle light, three green and three red lights are all out; flaps up: check the flap gauge; airspeed: read directly from the airspeed indicator after the flap gauge is crosschecked.
common_errors: Raising gear/flaps without a positive climb rate or before engine instruments are checked within limits — "Gear and flap retraction should be a conscious, deliberate act."
Moving the gear handle without the intercockpit "gear clear" call and momentary pause.
On student presolo contact sorties, the student raising the gear before the IP acknowledges "gear clear" with "clear".
Failing to confirm gear warning lights extinguished and flaps up before the 147 KIAS gear/flap airspeed limit.
Not applying nose-down trim as airspeed increases, leaving pressure on the control stick.
Climbing at maximum-rate pitch (nose as high as 12°) so that forward visibility is restricted, instead of accelerating to the normal 160-180 KIAS climb-out.
corrections: As airspeed increases, apply nose-down trim to relieve pressure on the control stick.
Normally accelerate to 160-180 KIAS during climb out to allow the nose to be lower and improve forward visibility.
Verbally confirm the A/C is cleaned up by gear/flap limiting airspeed.
sections.notes: The source text renders the normal climb-out speed as "16 0-180 KIAS" (extraction artifact of 160-180 KIAS); verbatim preserved as printed. DERIVED COMMON ERRORS: Chapter 4 publishes no "Common Errors" block; the common_errors listed here are derived by inverting the imperatives of the source text and are not a verbatim manual list.

sections.title: AFTER BECOMING AIRBORNE (CROSSWIND)
sections.technique_summary: Control inputs change significantly as the A/C leaves the ground. Crosswind controls must be released after takeoff, as the A/C is allowed to crab into the wind, to prevent the upwind wing from dipping towards the ground. Rudder requirements change as the wheels leave the ground, airspeed increases, and the A/C crabs into the wind. Climb in coordinated flight and maintain runway alignment on takeoff leg.
procedure_steps: Release the crosswind controls after takeoff.
Allow the A/C to crab into the wind.
Adjust rudder as the wheels leave the ground, airspeed increases and the A/C crabs into the wind.
Climb in coordinated flight and maintain runway alignment on takeoff leg.
common_errors: Holding crosswind controls after takeoff instead of releasing them, so the upwind wing dips towards the ground.
Not climbing in coordinated flight / failing to maintain runway alignment on takeoff leg.
corrections: Crosswind controls must be released after takeoff and the A/C allowed to crab into the wind, to prevent the upwind wing from dipping towards the ground.
Climb in coordinated flight and maintain runway alignment on takeoff leg.
sections.notes: Figure 4.3 "Crabbing Into Crosswind After Takeoff" is on PDF page 61 (printed 51) and is image-only. DERIVED COMMON ERRORS: Chapter 4 publishes no "Common Errors" block; the common_errors listed here are derived by inverting the imperatives of the source text and are not a verbatim manual list.

sections.title: ABNORMAL PROCEDURES — TAKEOFF ABORTS
sections.technique_summary: If there is reason to ABORT the takeoff, do not hesitate to do so. If the PNF sees something hazardous should inform the PF. If the A/C Commander (AC) is not flying during a time-critical situation that requires immediate action, and there is no time to relay this to the PF, the AC should take control of the A/C and accomplish the appropriate procedures.
procedure_steps: If there is reason to ABORT the takeoff, do not hesitate to do so.
PNF informs the PF upon seeing something hazardous.

If the AC is not flying during a time-critical situation requiring immediate action and there is no time to relay it to the PF, the AC takes control of the A/C and accomplishes the appropriate procedures.
common_errors: Hesitating to abort when there is reason to ABORT the takeoff.
PNF failing to inform the PF after seeing something hazardous.
corrections: Do not hesitate to abort when there is reason to.
In a time-critical situation with no time to relay to the PF, the A/C Commander takes control and accomplishes the appropriate procedures.
sections.notes: contact-39 (EMERGENCY PROCEDURES) is mapped here because an abort is an immediate-action procedure executed per Check List. DERIVED COMMON ERRORS: Chapter 4 publishes no "Common Errors" block; the common_errors listed here are derived by inverting the imperatives of the source text and are not a verbatim manual list.

sections.title: ABNORMAL PROCEDURES — WAKE TURBULENCE
sections.technique_summary: Anticipate wake turbulence when taking off behind other A/C on the same or parallel runways, especially if the wind is calm or straight down the runway. Wake turbulence is formed when an A/C is creating lift, therefore plan to take off at a point prior to the preceding A/C's take-off point or after their point of touchdown.
procedure_steps: Anticipate wake turbulence when taking off behind other A/C on the same or parallel runways, especially if the wind is calm or straight down the runway.
Plan to take off at a point prior to the preceding A/C's take-off point, or after their point of touchdown.
common_errors: Failing to anticipate wake turbulence when taking off behind other A/C on the same or parallel runways, especially with calm wind or wind straight down the runway.
Taking off past the preceding A/C's take-off point (and before their point of touchdown), i.e. into the wake.
corrections: Plan to take off at a point prior to the preceding A/C's take-off point or after their point of touchdown.
sections.notes: Wake-turbulence avoidance by choosing the takeoff point is preventive takeoff planning, not an emergency procedure, so contact-39 (EMERGENCY PROCEDURES) is not mapped here — it is mapped only in §4.7.1; contact-02 (TAKE OFF) covers this content. DERIVED COMMON ERRORS: Chapter 4 publishes no "Common Errors" block; the common_errors listed here are derived by inverting the imperatives of the source text and are not a verbatim manual list.

sections.title: TURNS AFTER TAKEOFF
sections.technique_summary: Climb straight ahead until past the departure end of the runway (or as directed). Attain a minimum of 140 KIAS and 700 feet AGL (local directives) before the first turn after takeoff.

parameters.name: minimum airspeed before first turn after takeoff
parameters.verbatim: Attain a minimum of 140 KIAS and 700 feet AGL (local directives) before the first turn after takeoff.

parameters.name: minimum altitude before first turn after takeoff
parameters.verbatim: Attain a minimum of 140 KIAS and 700 feet AGL (local directives) before the first turn after takeoff.

procedure_steps: Climb straight ahead until past the departure end of the runway (or as directed).
Attain a minimum of 140 KIAS and 700 feet AGL before the first turn after takeoff.
common_errors: Turning before passing the departure end of the runway (or before directed).
Turning below the minimum 140 KIAS and/or below 700 feet AGL.
sections.notes: The first turn after takeoff is already a departure phase, hence instrument-03 (STANDARD INSTRUMENT DEPARTURE) is mapped alongside instrument-02, mirroring contact-02 + contact-03. DERIVED COMMON ERRORS: Chapter 4 publishes no "Common Errors" block; the common_errors listed here are derived by inverting the imperatives of the source text and are not a verbatim manual list.

sections.title: CLIMBS
sections.technique_summary: Objective is to establish the A/C in a climb as required by local directives or published departure. Accelerate to climb airspeed 140-180 KIAS in accordance with local directives, power as required (normally MAX), pitch as required to fly the desired airspeed (normally 10-15°). Climbout airspeeds below 160 KIAS are permitted by the flight manual, but not normally recommended due to high pitch attitudes that limit forward visibility. Initiate the climb check in accordance with the flight manual passing 10.000 feet MSL.

parameters.name: climb airspeed
parameters.verbatim: a. Airspeed – Accelerate to climb airspeed 140-180 KIAS in accordance with local directives

parameters.name: climb power
parameters.verbatim: b. Power – As required, normally MAX

parameters.name: climb pitch
parameters.verbatim: c. Pitch – As required to fly desired airspeed (normally 10-15°)

parameters.name: minimum recommended climbout airspeed
parameters.verbatim: Climbout airspeeds below 160 KIAS are permitted by the flight manual, but not normally recommended due to high pitch attitudes that limit forward visibility.

parameters.name: climb check altitude
parameters.verbatim: Initiate the climb check in accordance with the flight manual passing 10.000 feet MSL.

parameters.name: climb gradient for 10° nose-high
parameters.value: approximately 1000 feet per nautical mile (1:1 ratio)
parameters.verbatim: A climb attitude of 10° nose-high results in a climb gradient of approximately 1000 feet per nautical mile (or what is referred to as a 1:1 ratio).

parameters.name: climb gradient rule of thumb
parameters.verbatim: This climb gradient is determined by using the formula that 1 degree is equal to 100 feet per nautical mile.

parameters.name: level flight pitch attitude at 160 KIAS
parameters.verbatim: Level flight for 160 KIAS is about 2-3° nose-high.

parameters.name: pitch above level flight for 1000 ft/NM climb
parameters.value: about 8° above level flight (10° pitch, 160 KIAS)
parameters.verbatim: Therefore a pitch attitude of 10° is about 8° above level flight (for 160 KIAS) resulting in 1000 feet per nautical mile climb rate.

parameters.name: level-off lead point
parameters.value: approximately 10 % of the VSI (e.g. 200 feet below at 2.000 fpm)
parameters.verbatim: One technique is to use a lead point that is approximately 10 % of the VSI. For example, if climbing at a rate of 2.000 fpm, start the level-off 200 feet below the desired altitude.

procedure_steps: Accelerate to climb airspeed 140-180 KIAS in accordance with local directives; power as required, normally MAX; pitch as required to fly the desired airspeed (normally 10-15°).
Initiate the climb check in accordance with the flight manual passing 10.000 feet MSL.

Straight climb from level flight: advance PCL and increase A/C pitch; if above the desired climb speed, initially set the pitch to achieve the desired airspeed; after reaching the desired airspeed, lower the nose to keep airspeed constant as altitude increases.
Make all pitch changes using outside references when available.
Maintain heading using section lines, a prominent point or object near the horizon, or other outside references crosschecked with the heading on the EHSI.
Maintain wings-level attitude by outside references crosschecked with the attitude indicator.
Trim after power is set and the climbing attitude is established; trimming is a continuous process throughout the climb and level off.

Climbing turns: if standard bank angles are not required to comply with published routings, use shallow-banked turns to maintain a higher rate of climb; trim used in the turn must be taken out during the rollout.

Level-off: start the level-off at a lead point that allows a smooth transition to the desired level-off altitude (technique: approximately 10 % of the VSI); at the lead point smoothly lower the nose to level flight; approaching the desired airspeed adjust the PCL to obtain the desired airspeed and trim the A/C.
Conduct an operations check (OPS check) at initial level-off and periodically throughout the flight, according to the flight manual.
common_errors: Climbing out below 160 KIAS: permitted by the flight manual, but not normally recommended due to high pitch attitudes that limit forward visibility.
Failing to lower the nose after reaching the desired airspeed, so airspeed does not stay constant as altitude increases.
Making pitch changes on instruments instead of outside references when outside references are available.
Not trimming after power is set and the climbing attitude is established — trimming is a continuous process throughout the climb and level off.
Failing to take out the trim used in a climbing turn during the rollout.
Using standard/steeper bank angles when not required by published routings, reducing rate of climb.
Starting the level-off without an adequate lead point, so the transition to the level-off altitude is not smooth.
Omitting the operations check at initial level-off and periodically throughout the flight.
corrections: If above the desired climb speed, initially set the pitch to achieve the desired airspeed; after reaching the desired airspeed, lower the nose to keep airspeed constant as altitude increases.
Crosscheck heading on the EHSI against outside references; crosscheck wings level against the attitude indicator.
Trim used in the turn must be taken out during the rollout.
Use a level-off lead point of approximately 10 % of the VSI; at the lead point smoothly lower the nose to level flight, then adjust PCL to the desired airspeed and trim.
sections.notes: Manual heading is "4.9. Climbs" (title kept verbatim); climbing turns and level-off are sub-techniques §4.9.4.b and §4.9.4.c and are included in this section's content. MAPPING: the whole section lies beyond the scope of the TAKE OFF items (contact-02 execution runs only "b/ Brakes release until the acceleration of the A/C up to the standard climb airspeed" ... "e/ Acceleration of the A/C to the standard climb airspeed"), so instrument-03 (SID — execution "SP executes climb and SID.") and instrument-07 (CONSTANT AIRSPEED - CONSTANT RATE CLIMBS / DESCENTS AND VERTICAL "S") are mapped instead of instrument-02, matching contact-03 / vfr_navigation-04. Figure 4.4 "Constant Airspeed Climb Pitch Attitudes" (PDF page 63, printed 53) is image-only; the numeric pitch/gradient relationships in the body text are captured above. sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.technique_summary: In any traffic pattern the runway is the primary visual reference. Each airfield has specific procedures designed to help prevent conflicts, assign traffic priority, and maximize training.
procedure_steps: Use the runway as the primary visual reference in any traffic pattern.
Fly the airfield-specific procedures that prevent conflicts, assign traffic priority, and maximize training.
sections.notes: Chapter-opening paragraph; no numeric parameters.

sections.title: LETDOWN AND TRAFFIC ENTRY
sections.technique_summary: Objective: descend and enter the traffic pattern. Letdown is the transition from the enroute structure to the traffic pattern. In busy environments detailed procedures are used for traffic sequencing and deconfliction. Strive to make all radio calls at the proper location; however, if deviations occur, always report actual location.

parameters.name: letdown airspeed
parameters.verbatim: Airspeed - 200 to 250 KIAS in accordance with local directives.

parameters.name: power / speed brake
parameters.verbatim: Power - As required. Speed brake as required.

parameters.name: pitch
parameters.verbatim: Pitch - As required to meet altitude restrictions.

parameters.name: crosswind estimation rule
parameters.verbatim: Use the 60 to 1 rule to determine crosswind component (crosswind = airspeed in miles per minute time multiplied by drift correction in degrees equals crab).

parameters.name: headwind estimation
parameters.verbatim: The difference between GPS groundspeed and indicated airspeed is approximately equal to the headwind component.

procedure_steps: Comply with published routing and altitude restrictions.
Monitor ATIS, if available.
Clear pattern entry route.
Set UHF/VHF to proper frequencies.
Consider surface wind effects on pattern and landing; anticipate crab and crosswind control requirements.
common_errors: Making radio calls at other than the proper location without reporting the actual location.
Assuming surface winds equal winds at pattern altitude ('Surface winds may differ from winds at pattern altitude').
corrections: If deviations occur, always report actual location.
Use clearing turns during VMC letdown to improve clearing, control of descent rate, and focus on outside visual references.
Use crab or drift correction and GPS groundspeed, at pattern altitude, to estimate pattern winds.
sections.notes: Drift correction is defined as the number of degrees off runway heading required to maintain constant ground track.

sections.title: A/C CONFIGURATION
sections.technique_summary: Three configurations are used in the T-6 and the same glide path is used for all flap settings. Touch-and-go landings are practiced at any flap setting; normally full stop landings are performed with flaps at Landing (LDG). Each configuration has its own base-turn and final airspeeds, and in gusty winds one-half the gust (max 10 KIAS) is added to final approach and touchdown speeds.

parameters.name: gust correction (all configurations)
parameters.verbatim: When flying in gusty winds, add one-half the gust up to a maximum of 10 KIAS to final approach and touchdown speeds.

parameters.name: Gear Down / Flaps LDG - base turn
parameters.verbatim: Base turn - 110 KIAS minimum (no less than ON-SPEED AOA indication).

parameters.name: Gear Down / Flaps LDG - final airspeed
parameters.verbatim: Final airspeed - 100 KIAS.

parameters.name: LDG flaps - runway length criterion
parameters.verbatim: LDG flaps should be used for full stop landings when landing distance is equal to or greater than 80 % of runway length.

parameters.name: LDG flaps - training crosswind limit
parameters.verbatim: Landing flaps should not be used in the training environment for landings with crosswinds greater than 10 KIAS because of the potential stresses the side loads impart on the landing gear.

parameters.name: LDG flaps - emergency crosswind limit
parameters.verbatim: If an emergency exists, the crosswind limit for land flaps is 25 KIAS.

parameters.name: Gear Down / Flaps TO - base turn
parameters.verbatim: Base turn - 115 KIAS minimum (no less than ON-SPEED AOA indication).

parameters.name: Gear Down / Flaps TO - final airspeed
parameters.verbatim: Final airspeed - 105 KIAS.

parameters.name: TO flaps - normal use
parameters.value: touch-and-go landings; full stop if landing distance not a factor
parameters.verbatim: Normally used for touch-and-go landings. May also be used for full stop landings if landing distance not a factor.

parameters.name: TO flaps - crosswind use
parameters.verbatim: Normally used for full stop landings with 10 knot or greater crosswind. May be used for full stop landing gusty winds.

parameters.name: Gear Down / Flaps UP - base turn
parameters.verbatim: Base turn - 120 KIAS minimum (no less than ON-SPEED AOA indication).

parameters.name: Gear Down / Flaps UP - final airspeed
parameters.verbatim: Final airspeed - 110 KIAS.

parameters.name: Flaps UP - crosswind use
parameters.verbatim: May be used for full stop landings with high crosswinds (greater than 20 KIAS) if landing distance is not a factor.

procedure_steps: Select the configuration appropriate to landing distance required, crosswind, and gust conditions.
Fly the base-turn and final airspeeds for the selected configuration, never slower than ON-SPEED AOA indication.
In gusty winds add one-half the gust (max 10 KIAS) to final approach and touchdown speeds.
common_errors: Using LDG flaps in gusty wind conditions ('Not recommended in gusty wind conditions').
Using LDG flaps in the training environment with crosswinds greater than 10 KIAS.
Flying the configuration airspeed while slower than ON-SPEED AOA indication.
corrections: Cross-check airspeed with AOA; never fly slower than the ON-SPEED AOA indication in the base turn.
sections.notes: Aerodynamic comparison given by the manual: LDG flaps generate significantly more drag than TO flaps and require the lowest pitch attitude and highest power setting of the three configurations to maintain level flight; LDG flaps decrease stall speed and reduce landing distance. TO flaps give slightly less lift but much less drag, providing the highest lift-to-drag ratio, with slightly higher stall speed and slightly longer landing distance than LDG flaps. Flaps UP generates the lowest amount of lift, requires the lowest power but the highest pitch attitude, has a stall speed higher than TO flaps and a significantly longer landing distance than LDG or TO flaps.

sections.title: OVERHEAD PATTERN AND LANDING
sections.technique_summary: The 360-degree overhead pattern is used to safely accommodate a maximum number of A/C with minimum congestion. Pattern spacing is adjusted for wind conditions. Figure 5.1 depicts the normal traffic pattern and Table 5.1 lists the overhead pattern parameters for each of the three configurations.

parameters.name: pattern type
parameters.verbatim: The 360° overhead pattern is used to safely accommodate a maximum number of A/C with minimum congestion.

parameters.name: gear extension speed (Figure 5.1)
parameters.verbatim: Lower gear below 147KIAS

parameters.name: downwind deceleration (Figure 5.1)
parameters.verbatim: Slow to 120KIAS minimum

parameters.name: final turn minimum by configuration (Figure 5.1)
parameters.verbatim: 120 (UP) 115(TO) 110(LDG) In turn, No slower than On-speed AOA

parameters.name: Table 5.1 - downwind KIAS (min)
parameters.verbatim: DOWNWIND 1 KIAS (min) 120

parameters.name: Table 5.1 - downwind torque
parameters.verbatim: 2 Torque 30-35%

parameters.name: Table 5.1 - downwind pitch attitude (level flight)
parameters.value: 1/4 ground, 3/4 sky (LDG and TO); spinner on horizon (UP)
parameters.verbatim: 3 Pitch attitude (level flight) 1/4 ground, 3/4 sky | 1/4 ground, 3/4 sky | Spinner on horizon

parameters.name: Table 5.1 - final turn KIAS
parameters.verbatim: FINAL TURN 5 KIAS 110 Minimum (No less than ON – SPEED AOA Indicator) | 115 Minimum | 120 Minimum

parameters.name: Table 5.1 - final turn torque
parameters.verbatim: 6 Torque Approx 18% | Approx 15% | Approx 12%

parameters.name: Table 5.1 - final turn pitch attitude
parameters.verbatim: 8 Pitch Attitude 2/3 Ground, 1/3 sky | 2/3 Ground, 1/3 sky | ½ Ground, ½ sky

parameters.name: Table 5.1 - final KIAS (min)
parameters.verbatim: FINAL 9 KIAS (Min)(Note 1) 100 (or AOA) | 105 (or AOA) | 110 (or AOA)

parameters.name: Table 5.1 - final torque
parameters.verbatim: 10 Torque Approx 16-18% | Approx 14-16% | Approx 12-14%

parameters.name: Table 5.1 - final pitch attitude
parameters.value: aim point 1/2 upwind screen (LDG, TO); 1/3 upwind screen (UP)
parameters.verbatim: 11 Pitch Attitude Aim point 1/2 upwind screen | Aim point 1/2 upwind screen | Aim point 1/3 upwind screen

parameters.name: Table 5.1 - touchdown KIAS target
parameters.verbatim: TOUCHDOWN 13 KIAS (Note1- 2) Target 80 | 85 | 90

parameters.name: Table 5.1 - target touchdown zone
parameters.verbatim: 14 Target touchdown zone (Note 3) 500-1000 feet down | 500-1000 feet down | 500-1500 feet down

parameters.name: Table 5.1 Note 1 - gust correction
parameters.verbatim: 1. Add ½ the gust component up to 10 KIAS to final approach speeds.

parameters.name: Table 5.1 Note 2 - speed increments
parameters.verbatim: 2. Factors such as A/C weight, crosswind and outside air temperature may increase these speeds slightly.

procedure_steps: Adjust pattern spacing for wind conditions.
Fly the configuration-specific airspeeds, torque settings, and pitch pictures of Table 5.1 at downwind, final turn, final, and touchdown.
Plan the touchdown in the target touchdown zone for the configuration flown.
common_errors: Routinely landing in the first few feet or 1.000 feet down the runway ('This does not mean that routinely landing in the first few feet or 1.000 feet down the runway is acceptable').
corrections: Select a proper touchdown point that has an adequate safety margin against landing short, yet allows the A/C to easily stop within the available runway.
sections.notes: Section number taken from the manual Table of Contents (5.4 OVERHEAD PATTERN AND LANDING); in the body of the manual this paragraph is unnumbered and the following paragraph is misnumbered '5.4. Initial Point (IP)'. Row 4 of Table 5.1, 'Runway spacing (No wind)', carries no readable value in the extracted PDF text (the cell content is graphical); the corresponding information is given in 5.7.3.4: 'No wind spacing is approximately 1/2 mile.'

sections.title: INITIAL POINT (IP)
sections.technique_summary: Objective: align the A/C with the landing runway. The IP is flown level at pattern altitude prescribed by the local LAP with pitch as required for level flight.

parameters.name: IP airspeed
parameters.verbatim: Airspeed: 200 KIAS.

parameters.name: IP power
parameters.verbatim: Power: 50 percent + 1 percent per 1,000 feet MSL altitude.

parameters.name: IP pitch
parameters.verbatim: Pitch: As required for level flight.

parameters.name: IP altitude
parameters.verbatim: Altitude: Fly the pattern as described in the local LAP.

procedure_steps: Align the A/C with the landing runway.
Set 200 KIAS with power of 50 percent plus 1 percent per 1,000 feet MSL altitude.
Hold pattern altitude as described in the local LAP with pitch as required for level flight.
sections.notes: Numbered 5.4 in the body of the manual but 5.5 (I.P.) in the Table of Contents; the pitch and altitude sub-paragraphs appear in the body under the 5.5 'Break' heading.

sections.title: BREAK
sections.technique_summary: Objective: transition from IP to downwind by a 180-degree level decelerating turn. Clear in the direction of turn, smoothly roll into 45 to 60 degrees of bank while adjusting the PCL, and fly a level decelerating turn to inside downwind, trimming control stick forces as airspeed decreases.

parameters.name: break airspeed schedule
parameters.verbatim: Airspeed - Slow from 200 KIAS to 120-147 KIAS.

parameters.name: break power
parameters.verbatim: Power - As required (approximately 10 %).

parameters.name: FCP visual reference
parameters.verbatim: FCP visual reference - Drag IFF antenna across horizon.

parameters.name: break zone
parameters.value: approach end to 3.000 feet down the runway
parameters.verbatim: The break zone is between the approach end and 3.000 feet down the runway.

parameters.name: bank angle
parameters.verbatim: Smoothly roll into 45° to 60° of bank and simultaneously adjust the PCL as required (approximately 10 %).

parameters.name: inside downwind speed
parameters.verbatim: On inside downwind continue to slow to 120-147 KIAS.

parameters.name: late break airspeed
parameters.verbatim: If required to break beyond normal break point, maintain airspeed (200 KIAS) until you break and lower gear at mid-field downwind to aid traffic pattern spacing.

procedure_steps: Clear in the direction of turn.
Smoothly roll into 45 to 60 degrees of bank and simultaneously adjust the PCL as required (approximately 10 %).
Fly a level, decelerating 180-degree turn to inside downwind, trimming control stick forces as airspeed decreases.
On inside downwind continue to slow to 120-147 KIAS.
If breaking beyond the normal break point, maintain 200 KIAS until the break and lower the gear at mid-field downwind.
common_errors: Breaking outside the break zone without adjusting for wind conditions and traffic spacing.
Failing to vary angle of bank and backpressure with wind conditions ('Angle of bank and backpressure vary with wind conditions').
corrections: Adjust the actual break point for wind conditions and traffic spacing; tower controllers may direct a break at a certain point within or outside the break zone.

sections.title: DOWNWIND
sections.technique_summary: Objective: maintain proper spacing and a ground track parallel to the runway. Apply drift correction and offset the inside/closed downwind ground track into the wind to account for the effects of wind on the final turn. Arrive at the perch point at 120 KIAS minimum, properly configured and ready to perform a planned 30-degree bank final turn.

parameters.name: downwind airspeed
parameters.verbatim: Description. Airspeed - 120 KIAS minimum.

parameters.name: gear clear call speed gate
parameters.verbatim: On downwind, with airspeed below 147 KIAS, make an inter-cockpit "gear clear" call and pause momentarily before moving the gear handle.

parameters.name: downwind torque
parameters.verbatim: Adjust power (approximately 30-35% Torque) to maintain airspeed (120 KIAS minimum) and pattern altitude.

parameters.name: no-wind spacing
parameters.verbatim: No wind spacing is approximately ½ mile.
